crm_notes: Customer profile: mid-late stage search platform for enterprise clients (legal, finance, healthcare). Heavy emphasis on SLA + residency.
Primary ask: build a RAG-enabled enterprise search layer that supports 100M–1B vectors with cost target <= $0.0004 per query at steady state.
Workloads: nightly bulk ingestion + continuous small updates (append + re-encode), heavy read/query traffic during business hours (spiky).
Indexing plan: plan to store mixed modal vectors (text + small images). Expecting ~600M vectors after year 1 expansion.
Searching stack: approximate NN (HNSW) for recall, two-stage reranker on GPU for precision-sensitive responses. Want Redwood to host reranker or provide private dedicated cluster.
Latency target: end-to-end (ANN + topK rerank) p95 < 150ms for enterprise SLA customers; p99 goal for premium tier.
Cost optimization asks: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, compact quantized vectors (4-bit/8-bit), cache warmup strategies, and suggestion of cheaper model variants for fallback.
POC success metrics: cost-per-query, p95/p99 latencies, ingestion throughput (vectors/day), and query QPS at target latency with 99% availability.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-10): 'We need something that scales like a search engine but behaves like a managed API — low ops burden.'
Notes: they run internal FAISS + Milvus tests; primary pain is ops complexity and unpredictable unit costs at scale. Redwood positioning = dedicated + optimize.
Ask: provide detailed cost model (per-token + per-rerank GPU second + storage for 600M vectors) and recommended autoscale policy for bursts up to 3x baseline QPS.
Next logistics: provision test dedicated pool (2x H100 equiv) for 2-week stress run; Redwood to instrument tracing and cost telemetry per route.
Short term blocker: procurement needs a pilot SOW and SOC2 attestation copy; security needs encryption at rest + KMS integration confirmed.
